newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian fighter flies low over fighting.
newsitem.headline: Albanian fighter flies low over fighting.

text.p: An Albanian fighter flew low over a southern village where fighting was taking place between insurgents and army units on Wednesday and smoke rose from the area just after it passed, eyewitnesses said.
The Russian-designed MiG fighter made its run near the village of Livina, about 10 km (six miles) east of Albania's southern coastal town of Sarande.
It was unclear whether the plane had dropped bombs on the area or crashed, the eyewitnesses said.
Albanian insurgents and army units fought in the southern region between Sarande and Delvine, 20 km (12 miles) to the east, throughout the morning, eyewitnesses said.
They said the army appeared to be moving to stamp out the insurrection in the south, which broke out after widespread rioting over the weekend.
Hospital officials in Sarande told Reuters by telephone that four people had been brought in with bullet wounds. One was in serious condition.

Anti-government riots swept the area over the weekend and local people seized hundreds of weapons from state armouries. The security forces were driven out of the southern region during the weekend clashes.
The insurgents have defied a state of emergency imposed on Sunday by the government and an accompanying shoot-on-sight order for anyone in the streets with unauthorised weapons.
Albania has been rocked by anti-government protests and violence since January when five "get-rich-quick" investment schemes collapsed, wiping out millions of dollars worth of savings.
Protesters have blamed President Sali Berisha for permitting the unregulated schemes to flourish and for failing to warn them of the risks.
